text:
alyssa: heads-up - our canary for release/helm-chart v3.4.1 is hanging in post-upgrade hook in eu-west-1.
marvin: seeing the same, job 'migrate-crds' is Pending for 45m
sami: logs show it waiting on leader-election for the crd controller? weird
alyssa: exact error from the hook pod:
```
I0621 12:10:03.123456 1 leaderelection.go:243] attempting to acquire leader lease...
E0621 12:15:03.123456 1 migration.go:78] failed to update CRD status: operation timeout: resource is locked by finalizer: "gpu.finalizers.redwood.ai"
```
kevin: so the hook tries to modify CRD status but some finalizer lock isn't cleared. Could be controller crash loop or controller leader held on another cluster node
marvin: also noticed autoscaler scaled up a gpu node but it has taint `gpu=reserved:NoSchedule` so the hook job couldn't land there (it needs toleration?).
infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: added 1 n1-standard-8 (gpu-pool) to eu-west-1-gpu-pool
sami: the job is non-privileged, expects to run on cpu nodes. Why would it be scheduled to gpu nodes? scheduler Predicates show insufficient cpu on cpu pool
alyssa: TL;DR: migration job in post-upgrade hook is stuck waiting on CRD status update because controller that removes finalizer is leader-elected on a drained node; scheduler can't place job on cpu nodes due to resource fragmentation; autoscaler adds gpu node (tainted), not helpful.
marvin: steps I tried:
- `kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep redwood-controller` -> one replica CrashLoopBackOff on node `ip-10-0-7-12` (cordoned)
- tried `kubectl uncordon ip-10-0-7-12` but it was cordoned by cluster-autoscaler reclaim
kevin: repo helm chart has hook annotated with `helm.sh/hook-weight: "10"` and no tolerations, so it can't run on tainted gpupool. We have a mismatch: the hook should be able to schedule on control-plane or cpu nodes.
alyssa: workaround proposal: cancel the release rollout so Helm doesn't wait, manually patch CRD finalizer to remove lock, restart controller pod, then re-run helm upgrade
sami: manual patch command:
```
kubectl -n redwood patch crd redwoodgpus.mycompany.com -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge
```
marvin: patching finalizers is risky but acceptable for emergency. We should record all steps in ticket.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: noticed gitops sync failed for `ops/helm/releases` - repo is in a 'blocked' state
kevin: also worth noting: our GitOps automation disallows force-rollbacks for canary releases. That prevented the autosync rollback. Need a short-term escape hatch in automation.
alyssa: cost note: stuck GPU node is billed; current estimate ~ $4.8/hr while this is unresolved. Pinged infra-costs channel.
marvin: I'm going to patch finalizer and restart controller. Sami, can you open a temporary exempt PR to allow force-rollback for this release? tag: @devops
sami: opening PR now -> https://git.internal/repo/ops/helm/releases/pulls/487
sami: PR description includes rollback escape hatch with audit logging and TTL
kevin: once controller is back, we should ensure the hook has tolerations: add `tolerations: - key: "gpu" operator: "Exists" effect: "NoSchedule"` and mount nodeSelector for cpu preference
alyssa: agreed. After we recover, let's add a pre-flight check to the CI pipeline to verify post-upgrade hooks are schedulable given current taints (run `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath` + dry-run scheduling via `kubectl debug --dry-run`)
marvin: after patch: controller restarted, finalizer removed, migration job completed in ~3m, helm upgrade proceeded to 80% canary
infra-bot: alert: canary success threshold reached for release v3.4.1
alyssa: follow-ups: (1) change hook tolerations in chart (PR #890), (2) add controller liveness to avoid long leader holds, (3) add GitOps escape hatch doc, (4) add cost alert for leaked GPU nodes
sami: filing postmortem and ops checklist now
marvin: thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: nice recovery. let's avoid manual finalizer patches next time, but good call for emergency
